title.ro: Cuvinte din viața de zi cu zi

text.ro: Învățăm cuvinte pe teme: familie (mother, father, sister), școală (pencil, desk), mâncare (soup, cake).
text.en: We learn words by topic: family (mother, father, sister), school (pencil, desk), food (soup, cake).

text.ro: Alte teme: casa (kitchen, sofa), animalele (horse, rabbit), corpul (head, hand) și hainele (jumper, trousers).
text.en: More topics: home (kitchen, sofa), animals (horse, rabbit), the body (head, hand) and clothes (jumper, trousers).

text.ro: Ajută să grupezi cuvintele pe teme și să le spui în propoziții: „My brother has a red jumper.”
text.en: It helps to group words by topic and to use them in sentences: "My brother has a red jumper."

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.vocab.topics.5
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: To be, have got și there is / there are
title.en: To be, have got and there is / there are

text.ro: To be: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we/you/they are. Întrebare: „Are you ten?” Negativ: „He is not (isn’t) at home.”
text.en: To be: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we/you/they are. Question: "Are you ten?" Negative: "He is not (isn’t) at home."

text.ro: Have got = a avea: „I have got a bike.” „She has got two brothers.” Întrebare: „Has he got a pen?”
text.en: Have got means "to have": "I have got a bike." "She has got two brothers." Question: "Has he got a pen?"

text.ro: There is + un singur lucru, there are + mai multe: „There is a book on the desk.” „There are five apples.” Negativ: „There isn’t any milk.”
text.en: There is + one thing, there are + more than one: "There is a book on the desk." "There are five apples." Negative: "There isn’t any milk."

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.tobe.5
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Folosim present simple pentru obiceiuri și fapte: „I play football on Sundays.” Verbul rămâne la forma de bază.
text.en: We use the present simple for habits and facts: "I play football on Sundays." The verb stays in its base form.

text.ro: La he / she / it adăugăm -s: „She plays.” După s, sh, ch, x, o adăugăm -es: „He watches TV.” „She goes.” Consoană + y devine -ies: „study – studies”.
text.en: With he / she / it we add -s: "She plays." After s, sh, ch, x, o we add -es: "He watches TV." "She goes." Consonant + y becomes -ies: "study – studies".

text.ro: Atenție: have devine has („He has a dog”). Nu spunem „He play”, ci „He plays”.
text.en: Careful: have becomes has ("He has a dog"). We do not say "He play" but "He plays".

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.present.5
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Pronume personale: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Ele sunt subiectul: „She is my friend.”
text.en: Subject pronouns: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. They are the subject: "She is my friend."

text.ro: După verb sau prepoziție folosim me, you, him, her, it, us, them: „Give it to me.” Posesive: my, your, his, her, its, our, their.
text.en: After a verb or preposition we use me, you, him, her, it, us, them: "Give it to me." Possessives: my, your, his, her, its, our, their.

text.ro: Posesorul se arată cu ’s: „my sister’s bag”. Aproape: this / these; departe: that / those.
text.en: The owner is shown with ’s: "my sister’s bag". Near: this / these; far: that / those.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.pronouns.5
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Întrebări și negații la present simple

text.ro: Întrebare: Do / Does + subiect + verb de bază: „Do you like pizza?” „Does she play chess?” Verbul nu mai are -s.
text.en: Question: Do / Does + subject + base verb: "Do you like pizza?" "Does she play chess?" The verb has no -s any more.

text.ro: Negativ: don’t / doesn’t + verb de bază: „I don’t like spiders.” „He doesn’t play chess.”
text.en: Negative: don’t / doesn’t + base verb: "I don’t like spiders." "He doesn’t play chess."

text.ro: Cuvinte interogative: What (ce), Where (unde), When (când), Who (cine), How many (câți): „Where does your uncle live?”
text.en: Question words: What, Where, When, Who, How many: "Where does your uncle live?"

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.questions.5
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Present continuous: ce se întâmplă acum
title.en: Present continuous: what is happening now

text.ro: Present continuous = am / is / are + verb cu -ing: „They are playing football.” Îl folosim pentru ce se întâmplă acum.
text.en: Present continuous = am / is / are + verb + -ing: "They are playing football." We use it for what is happening now.

text.ro: Ortografie: live – living (cade e), stop – stopping (se dublează consoana), run – running. Negativ: „She isn’t sleeping.”
text.en: Spelling: live – living (drop the e), stop – stopping (double the consonant), run – running. Negative: "She isn’t sleeping."

text.ro: Cuvinte-semnal: now, at the moment, Look!, Listen! Unele verbe nu se folosesc așa: like, want, know („I like pizza”, nu „I am liking”).
text.en: Signal words: now, at the moment, Look!, Listen! Some verbs are not used like this: like, want, know ("I like pizza", not "I am liking").

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.continuous.5
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: De obicei adăugăm -s: book – books, boy – boys. După s, sh, ch, x adăugăm -es: bus – buses, watch – watches.
text.en: Usually we add -s: book – books, boy – boys. After s, sh, ch, x we add -es: bus – buses, watch – watches.

text.ro: Consoană + y devine -ies: city – cities, baby – babies. La f / fe: leaf – leaves, knife – knives. Unele cu o: potato – potatoes, dar photo – photos.
text.en: Consonant + y becomes -ies: city – cities, baby – babies. With f / fe: leaf – leaves, knife – knives. Some with o: potato – potatoes, but photo – photos.

text.ro: Plurale neregulate (trebuie învățate): man – men, woman – women, child – children, foot – feet, tooth – teeth, sheep – sheep.
text.en: Irregular plurals (learn them): man – men, woman – women, child – children, foot – feet, tooth – teeth, sheep – sheep.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.plurals.5
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Articolul: a, an, the, some, any
title.en: Articles: a, an, the, some, any

text.ro: A înaintea unui sunet de consoană (a book, a university), an înaintea unui sunet de vocală (an apple, an hour). Contează sunetul, nu litera.
text.en: "A" comes before a consonant sound (a book, a university), "an" before a vowel sound (an apple, an hour). The sound matters, not the letter.

text.ro: The pentru ceva știut sau unic: „the sun”, „the cat from my garden”. Cu instrumente muzicale: „play the guitar”.
text.en: "The" is for something known or unique: "the sun", "the cat from my garden". With instruments: "play the guitar".

text.ro: Some în propoziții afirmative și oferte („some milk”), any în întrebări și negații („Is there any milk?” „We haven’t got any.”).
text.en: "Some" is for statements and offers ("some milk"), "any" for questions and negatives ("Is there any milk?" "We haven’t got any.").

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.articles.5
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Prepoziții de loc și de timp

text.ro: Loc: in (în), on (pe), under (sub), next to (lângă), between (între), in front of (în fața). „The ball is in the box.”
text.en: Place: in, on, under, next to, between, in front of. "The ball is in the box."

text.ro: Timp: at + ora (at seven o’clock), on + ziua (on Monday), in + luna / anotimpul (in June, in summer).
text.en: Time: at + clock time (at seven o’clock), on + day (on Monday), in + month / season (in June, in summer).

text.ro: Expresii fixe: at home, at school, at night, in the morning, on Saturday morning.
text.en: Fixed phrases: at home, at school, at night, in the morning, on Saturday morning.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.prep.5
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.en: How to read a short text

text.ro: Citește întâi tot textul o dată, fără să te oprești la fiecare cuvânt nou. Încearcă să înțelegi despre ce este vorba.
text.en: Read the whole text once without stopping at every new word. Try to understand what it is about.

text.ro: Apoi citește întrebarea și caută în text cuvintele ei: numere, nume, locuri. Răspunsul este de obicei în aceeași propoziție.
text.en: Then read the question and look for its key words in the text: numbers, names, places. The answer is usually in the same sentence.

text.ro: La adevărat / fals compară cu textul, nu cu ce crezi tu. Dacă textul spune altceva, răspunsul este fals.
text.en: For true / false compare with the text, not with what you think. If the text says something different, the answer is false.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.read.short.5
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Limbaj de zi cu zi: saluturi, prezentări, cumpărături

text.ro: Salut: Hello, Hi, Good morning, Goodbye, See you tomorrow. „How are you?” – „I’m fine, thanks.”
text.en: Greetings: Hello, Hi, Good morning, Goodbye, See you tomorrow. "How are you?" – "I’m fine, thanks."

text.ro: Prezentare: „This is my friend, Dan.” – „Nice to meet you.” – „Nice to meet you, too.” Mulțumesc: „Thank you.” – „You’re welcome.”
text.en: Introductions: "This is my friend, Dan." – "Nice to meet you." – "Nice to meet you, too." Thanks: "Thank you." – "You’re welcome."

text.ro: La magazin: „Can I help you?” „How much is it?” „I’d like a kilo of apples, please.” „Here you are.” Spunem mereu please.
text.en: In a shop: "Can I help you?" "How much is it?" "I’d like a kilo of apples, please." "Here you are." Always say please.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.func.basic.5
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Cuvinte noi: hobby-uri, meserii, oraș, călătorii
title.en: New words: hobbies, jobs, town, travel

text.ro: Hobby-uri (painting, fishing, hiking) și meserii (nurse, farmer, firefighter). „My uncle is a vet.”
text.en: Hobbies (painting, fishing, hiking) and jobs (nurse, farmer, firefighter). "My uncle is a vet."

text.ro: Orașul (bank, museum, bridge) și transportul (train, tram, lorry, underground). Atenție la engleza britanică: lorry, petrol, underground.
text.en: The town (bank, museum, bridge) and transport (train, tram, lorry, underground). Note British English: lorry, petrol, underground.

text.ro: Vremea (foggy, storm, rainbow) și călătoria (passport, suitcase, tourist). Învață cuvintele într-o propoziție, nu singure.
text.en: Weather (foggy, storm, rainbow) and travel (passport, suitcase, tourist). Learn words in a sentence, not alone.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.vocab.topics.6
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Past simple spune ce s-a întâmplat și s-a terminat: „I visited my aunt yesterday.” Forma este aceeași pentru toate persoanele.
text.en: The past simple says what happened and is finished: "I visited my aunt yesterday." The form is the same for all persons.

text.ro: Verbe regulate: + -ed (play – played), + -d (live – lived), consoană + y: -ied (study – studied), dublare: stop – stopped, travel – travelled.
text.en: Regular verbs: + -ed (play – played), + -d (live – lived), consonant + y: -ied (study – studied), doubling: stop – stopped, travel – travelled.

text.ro: Verbe neregulate (trebuie învățate): go – went, see – saw, eat – ate, buy – bought. Cuvinte-semnal: yesterday, last week, two days ago, in 2019.
text.en: Irregular verbs (learn them): go – went, see – saw, eat – ate, buy – bought. Signal words: yesterday, last week, two days ago, in 2019.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.past.6
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Verbele neregulate nu primesc -ed: go – went, come – came, make – made, take – took, give – gave. Nu există „goed” sau „buyed”.
text.en: Irregular verbs do not take -ed: go – went, come – came, make – made, take – took, give – gave. There is no "goed" or "buyed".

text.ro: Unele nu se schimbă: cut – cut, put – put, read – read (se scrie la fel, se pronunță „red”).
text.en: Some do not change: cut – cut, put – put, read – read (same spelling, pronounced "red").

text.ro: Învață-le în grupe cu sunet asemănător: buy – bought, bring – brought, think – thought; sing – sang, drink – drank, swim – swam.
text.en: Learn them in groups that sound alike: buy – bought, bring – brought, think – thought; sing – sang, drink – drank, swim – swam.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.irregular.6
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Întrebări și negații la past simple

text.ro: Întrebare: Did + subiect + verb de bază: „Did you watch the match?” Verbul revine la forma de bază, fără -ed.
text.en: Question: Did + subject + base verb: "Did you watch the match?" The verb goes back to the base form, without -ed.

text.ro: Negativ: didn’t + verb de bază: „She didn’t see the film.” Nu spunem „She didn’t saw”.
text.en: Negative: didn’t + base verb: "She didn’t see the film." We do not say "She didn’t saw".

text.ro: Cu was / were nu folosim did: „Were you at home?” „We weren’t there.” Întrebare cu cuvânt interogativ: „Where did they go?”
text.en: With was / were we do not use did: "Were you at home?" "We weren’t there." Question word + did: "Where did they go?"

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.pastq.6
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: De la mereu la niciodată: always (100%), usually, often, sometimes, rarely / hardly ever, never (0%).
text.en: From always to never: always (100%), usually, often, sometimes, rarely / hardly ever, never (0%).

text.ro: Poziție: înaintea verbului principal („I often walk”), dar după to be („She is never late”).
text.en: Position: before the main verb ("I often walk"), but after to be ("She is never late").

text.ro: Never are deja sens negativ: „I never eat fish.” (nu „I don’t never eat”). Întrebare: „How often do you play tennis?”
text.en: "Never" is already negative: "I never eat fish." (not "I don’t never eat"). Question: "How often do you play tennis?"

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.freq.6
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Past continuous: ce se petrecea atunci
title.en: Past continuous: what was happening then

text.ro: Past continuous = was / were + verb cu -ing: „At eight o’clock I was reading.” Arată o acțiune în desfășurare în trecut.
text.en: Past continuous = was / were + verb + -ing: "At eight o’clock I was reading." It shows an action in progress in the past.

text.ro: Was cu I / he / she / it, were cu you / we / they: „They were playing.” Negativ: „She wasn’t sleeping.”
text.en: "Was" with I / he / she / it, "were" with you / we / they: "They were playing." Negative: "She wasn’t sleeping."

text.ro: Cu while: „While I was cooking, the phone rang.” Acțiunea lungă este past continuous, cea scurtă care o întrerupe este past simple.
text.en: With "while": "While I was cooking, the phone rang." The long action is past continuous, the short one that interrupts it is past simple.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.pastcont.6
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Adjective scurte: -er / -est: tall – taller – the tallest. Terminate în e: nice – nicer – nicest. Dublare: big – bigger – biggest.
text.en: Short adjectives: -er / -est: tall – taller – the tallest. Ending in e: nice – nicer – nicest. Doubling: big – bigger – biggest.

text.ro: Consoană + y: happy – happier – happiest. Adjective lungi: more / most: beautiful – more beautiful – the most beautiful.
text.en: Consonant + y: happy – happier – happiest. Long adjectives: more / most: beautiful – more beautiful – the most beautiful.

text.ro: Neregulate: good – better – the best, bad – worse – the worst. Comparăm cu than: „Tom is taller than Dan.” Superlativ: „the tallest in the class”.
text.en: Irregular: good – better – the best, bad – worse – the worst. We compare with "than": "Tom is taller than Dan." Superlative: "the tallest in the class".

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.compar.6
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Numărabil, nenumărabil, some, any, much, many
title.en: Countable, uncountable, some, any, much, many

text.ro: Numărabile: a book, two books. Nenumărabile nu au plural și nu primesc a / an: water, milk, bread, money, information, advice.
text.en: Countable: a book, two books. Uncountable nouns have no plural and no a / an: water, milk, bread, money, information, advice.

text.ro: How many + numărabil plural („How many apples?”), how much + nenumărabil („How much water?”). În negații: „There isn’t much milk.”
text.en: How many + plural countable ("How many apples?"), how much + uncountable ("How much water?"). In negatives: "There isn’t much milk."

text.ro: a lot of merge cu ambele: „a lot of friends”, „a lot of traffic”. Some: afirmativ și oferte; any: întrebări și negații.
text.en: "A lot of" goes with both: "a lot of friends", "a lot of traffic". Some: statements and offers; any: questions and negatives.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.quantity.6
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Viitorul: will și be going to
title.en: The future: will and be going to

text.ro: Will + verb de bază: „It will be sunny tomorrow.” Pentru predicții, promisiuni și decizii luate acum. Negativ: won’t.
text.en: Will + base verb: "It will be sunny tomorrow." For predictions, promises and decisions made now. Negative: won’t.

text.ro: Be going to = am / is / are going to + verb: „We are going to visit Paris.” Pentru planuri făcute înainte și pentru ce se vede că urmează.
text.en: Be going to = am / is / are going to + verb: "We are going to visit Paris." For plans made earlier and for what we can see is coming.

text.ro: Atenție: nu punem -s după will („will plays” este greșit) și nu spunem „will to play”. Negativ: „He isn’t going to come.”
text.en: Careful: no -s after will ("will plays" is wrong) and no "will to play". Negative: "He isn’t going to come."

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.future.6
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Can = pot / știu: „I can swim.” Negativ: can’t. Could = trecut: „I could ride a bike at five.” Întrebare: „Can you help me?”
text.en: Can = ability: "I can swim." Negative: can’t. Could = past: "I could ride a bike at five." Question: "Can you help me?"

text.ro: Must / have to = obligație: „You must do your homework.” Mustn’t = interzis; don’t have to = nu este nevoie.
text.en: Must / have to = obligation: "You must do your homework." Mustn’t = forbidden; don’t have to = not necessary.

text.ro: Should = sfat: „You should go to bed early.” După modale folosim mereu verbul de bază, fără -s și fără to: „She can swim.”
text.en: Should = advice: "You should go to bed early." After modals we always use the base verb, without -s and without to: "She can swim."

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.modals.6
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Cum citim un text mai lung
title.en: How to read a longer text

text.ro: Textele povestesc adesea ce s-a întâmplat: caută verbele la trecut și ordinea întâmplărilor (first, then, after that).
text.en: Texts often tell what happened: look for past verbs and the order of events (first, then, after that).

text.ro: Subliniază mental cuvintele-cheie: cine, ce, când, unde. Întrebările urmează de obicei ordinea textului.
text.en: Mentally underline the key words: who, what, when, where. The questions usually follow the order of the text.

text.ro: Nu alege un răspuns doar pentru că are un cuvânt din text. Verifică dacă înseamnă același lucru cu ce spune textul.
text.en: Do not choose an answer just because it has a word from the text. Check that it means the same as what the text says.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.read.6
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Cerem politicos: „Excuse me, how do I get to the station?” sau „Where is the post office?”
text.en: We ask politely: "Excuse me, how do I get to the station?" or "Where is the post office?"

text.ro: Indicații: Go straight on (înainte), Turn left / right, Take the second turning, Cross the road, Walk along this street, at the traffic lights.
text.en: Directions: Go straight on, Turn left / right, Take the second turning, Cross the road, Walk along this street, at the traffic lights.

text.ro: Locuri: next to (lângă), opposite (vizavi), between (între), at the corner (la colț), near here (aproape). „It’s five minutes on foot.”
text.en: Places: next to, opposite, between, at the corner, near here. "It’s five minutes on foot."

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.func.directions.6
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Cuvinte noi: sănătate, mediu, tehnologie, sentimente
title.en: New words: health, environment, technology, feelings

text.ro: Sănătate (fever, cough, medicine, allergy) și cumpărături (receipt, discount, refund, queue).
text.en: Health (fever, cough, medicine, allergy) and shopping (receipt, discount, refund, queue).

text.ro: Mediu (pollution, recycling, energy, waste) și tehnologie (laptop, password, download, battery).
text.en: Environment (pollution, recycling, energy, waste) and technology (laptop, password, download, battery).

text.ro: Sentimente: excited, nervous, proud, worried, disappointed. „I felt nervous before the test.” Folosește-le în propoziții scurte.
text.en: Feelings: excited, nervous, proud, worried, disappointed. "I felt nervous before the test." Use them in short sentences.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.vocab.topics.7
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Verbele neregulate au trei forme: infinitiv, past simple, participiu trecut: write – wrote – written, take – took – taken.
text.en: Irregular verbs have three forms: base, past simple, past participle: write – wrote – written, take – took – taken.

text.ro: Uneori past simple și participiul sunt la fel: buy – bought – bought, make – made – made, have – had – had.
text.en: Sometimes the past simple and the participle are the same: buy – bought – bought, make – made – made, have – had – had.

text.ro: Altele diferă: go – went – gone, see – saw – seen, eat – ate – eaten. Participiul se folosește cu have / has („I have seen”) și la pasiv.
text.en: Others differ: go – went – gone, see – saw – seen, eat – ate – eaten. The participle is used with have / has ("I have seen") and in the passive.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.irregular.7
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Present perfect = have / has + participiu trecut: „I have finished my homework.” „She has lived here since 2019.”
text.en: Present perfect = have / has + past participle: "I have finished my homework." "She has lived here since 2019."

text.ro: Îl folosim pentru experiențe fără dată („I have never been to London”), pentru rezultate de acum („I have lost my keys”) și cu for / since.
text.en: We use it for experiences with no date ("I have never been to London"), for results now ("I have lost my keys") and with for / since.

text.ro: Cuvinte frecvente: ever, never, already, just, yet, so far. Negativ: haven’t / hasn’t. Întrebare: „Have you ever eaten sushi?”
text.en: Common words: ever, never, already, just, yet, so far. Negative: haven’t / hasn’t. Question: "Have you ever eaten sushi?"

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.perfect.7
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Egalitate: as + adjectiv + as: „My bag is as heavy as yours.” Negativ: „not as big as”.
text.en: Equality: as + adjective + as: "My bag is as heavy as yours." Negative: "not as big as".

text.ro: Comparativ cu than: „taller than”, „more interesting than”. Perechea: „The more you practise, the better you get.” Adverbe: „more carefully”.
text.en: Comparative with than: "taller than", "more interesting than". The pair: "The more you practise, the better you get." Adverbs: "more carefully".

text.ro: Too = prea mult (negativ): „too cold to swim”. Enough = suficient, vine după adjectiv: „tall enough”, „not old enough”.
text.en: Too = more than is good (negative): "too cold to swim". Enough = sufficient, after an adjective: "tall enough", "not old enough".

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.compar.7
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Will, going to sau present continuous?
title.en: Will, going to or present continuous?

text.ro: Will: predicții fără dovezi („I think it will rain”), promisiuni, decizii luate acum („I’ll open the window”).
text.en: Will: predictions without evidence ("I think it will rain"), promises, decisions made now ("I’ll open the window").

text.ro: Be going to: planuri făcute înainte („I’m going to study medicine”) și predicții cu dovezi („Look at those clouds! It’s going to rain.”).
text.en: Be going to: plans made before ("I’m going to study medicine") and predictions with evidence ("Look at those clouds! It’s going to rain.").

text.ro: Present continuous: aranjamente fixate („I’m meeting Dan at six”). Present simple: orare („The train leaves at seven”).
text.en: Present continuous: fixed arrangements ("I’m meeting Dan at six"). Present simple: timetables ("The train leaves at seven").

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.futureforms.7
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Propoziția afirmativă: subiect + verb + restul: „My brother plays football.” Timpul vine de obicei la sfârșit.
text.en: A statement: subject + verb + the rest: "My brother plays football." The time usually comes at the end.

text.ro: Întrebarea: (cuvânt interogativ) + auxiliar + subiect + verb: „Where did he go?” „Have you finished?” Subiectul vine după auxiliar.
text.en: A question: (question word) + auxiliary + subject + verb: "Where did he go?" "Have you finished?" The subject comes after the auxiliary.

text.ro: Negativul: subiect + auxiliar + not + verb: „We do not have to wear a uniform.” Prima literă mare arată începutul propoziției.
text.en: A negative: subject + auxiliary + not + verb: "We do not have to wear a uniform." The capital letter shows where the sentence starts.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.wordorder.7
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Past simple: acțiune încheiată la un moment precis din trecut: yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago. „I saw the film last week.”
text.en: Past simple: a finished action at a definite time in the past: yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago. "I saw the film last week."

text.ro: Present perfect: legătură cu prezentul, fără moment precis: „I have seen that film.” Cu since / for / so far / already / never.
text.en: Present perfect: a link with now, no definite time: "I have seen that film." With since / for / so far / already / never.

text.ro: Nu combinăm present perfect cu un moment încheiat: nu „I have seen it yesterday”, ci „I saw it yesterday”.
text.en: We do not combine the present perfect with a finished time: not "I have seen it yesterday" but "I saw it yesterday".

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.perfectvs.7
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Modale: may, might, could, had better
title.en: Modals: may, might, could, had better

text.ro: May / might = posibilitate: „It might rain later.” May cere și permisiune: „May I borrow your pen?”
text.en: May / might = possibility: "It might rain later." May also asks for permission: "May I borrow your pen?"

text.ro: Could = cerere politicoasă („Could you open the window?”) sau abilitate în trecut („I couldn’t swim”). Would you like…? = ofertă.
text.en: Could = polite request ("Could you open the window?") or past ability ("I couldn’t swim"). Would you like…? = offer.

text.ro: Mustn’t = interzis; don’t have to = nu e nevoie. Had better = sfat puternic: „You had better take a coat.” Shall we…? = sugestie.
text.en: Mustn’t = forbidden; don’t have to = not necessary. Had better = strong advice: "You had better take a coat." Shall we…? = suggestion.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.modals.7
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Un verb frazal = verb + particulă, cu alt sens: get up (a te ridica din pat), wake up (a te trezi), sit down, stand up.
text.en: A phrasal verb = verb + particle with a new meaning: get up, wake up, sit down, stand up.

text.ro: Alte exemple: turn on / off (a porni / a opri), put on / take off (a îmbrăca / a scoate), look for (a căuta), look after (a avea grijă).
text.en: More examples: turn on / off, put on / take off, look for (search), look after (take care of).

text.ro: Învață verbul frazal întreg, într-o propoziție: „Don’t give up!” „Let’s find out.” „Hurry up!”
text.en: Learn the whole phrasal verb in a sentence: "Don’t give up!" "Let’s find out." "Hurry up!"

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.phrasal.7
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Few + numărabil plural, little + nenumărabil. A few / a little = câțiva / puțin (suficient); few / little = aproape deloc.
text.en: Few + plural countable, little + uncountable. A few / a little = some (enough); few / little = hardly any.

text.ro: Too much + nenumărabil, too many + numărabil: „too much noise”, „too many cars”. Plenty of = din belșug. Enough: „enough food”.
text.en: Too much + uncountable, too many + countable: "too much noise", "too many cars". Plenty of = more than enough. Enough: "enough food".

text.ro: Every / each + singular („Every student has a locker”). All / both + plural („Both my parents work”).
text.en: Every / each + singular ("Every student has a locker"). All / both + plural ("Both my parents work").

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.quantifiers.7
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.en: How to read texts about experiences

text.ro: Observă timpurile: present perfect („has lived”) arată ce s-a întâmplat până acum, past simple („went”) un moment încheiat.
text.en: Notice the tenses: present perfect ("has lived") shows what has happened up to now, past simple ("went") a finished time.

text.ro: Caută cuvintele care leagă ideile: but, so, because, although, then. Ele arată cauza și rezultatul.
text.en: Look for the words that link ideas: but, so, because, although, then. They show cause and result.

text.ro: La o întrebare de inferență, răspunsul nu este scris cuvânt cu cuvânt, dar textul îl arată. Verifică mereu cu textul.
text.en: In an inference question the answer is not written word for word, but the text shows it. Always check against the text.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.read.7
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Invităm: „Would you like to come to my party?” „Do you want to come with us?” Sugerăm: „Let’s play football.” „Why don’t we go to the beach?” „How about going for a walk?”
text.en: Inviting: "Would you like to come to my party?" "Do you want to come with us?" Suggesting: "Let’s play football." "Why don’t we go to the beach?" "How about going for a walk?"

text.ro: Acceptăm: „Yes, I’d love to. Thank you!” „Good idea!” „Sure, no problem.”
text.en: Accepting: "Yes, I’d love to. Thank you!" "Good idea!" "Sure, no problem."

text.ro: Refuzăm politicos: „I’m sorry, I can’t. I have homework.” „I’m afraid I can’t.” „I’d rather play outside.” Spunem și motivul.
text.en: Refusing politely: "I’m sorry, I can’t. I have homework." "I’m afraid I can’t." "I’d rather play outside." Give a reason too.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.func.invitations.7
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Cuvinte noi: media, carieră, societate, știință, artă
title.en: New words: media, careers, society, science, arts

text.ro: Media (newspaper, headline, documentary, interview) și carieră (salary, employee, qualification, deadline).
text.en: Media (newspaper, headline, documentary, interview) and careers (salary, employee, qualification, deadline).

text.ro: Societate (community, volunteer, equality, citizen, tradition) și știință (experiment, invention, evidence, research).
text.en: Society (community, volunteer, equality, citizen, tradition) and science (experiment, invention, evidence, research).

text.ro: Artă (exhibition, orchestra, novel, performance, gallery). Grupează cuvintele pe teme și caută-le în texte.
text.en: Arts (exhibition, orchestra, novel, performance, gallery). Group words by topic and look for them in texts.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.vocab.topics.8
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Tip 0 (adevăruri generale): If + present, present: „If you heat ice, it melts.” Putem spune și „when”.
text.en: Type 0 (general truths): If + present, present: "If you heat ice, it melts." We can also say "when".

text.ro: Tip 1 (posibilitate reală în viitor): If + present simple, will + verb: „If it rains, we will stay at home.” Nu folosim will după if.
text.en: Type 1 (a real possibility in the future): If + present simple, will + verb: "If it rains, we will stay at home." We do not use will after if.

text.ro: Unless = if not: „I won’t go unless you come.” Virgula apare când propoziția cu if este prima: „If I see him, I’ll tell him.”
text.en: Unless = if not: "I won’t go unless you come." We use a comma when the if-clause comes first: "If I see him, I’ll tell him."

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.cond.8
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Pasivul: obiect + to be + participiu trecut (+ by agent): „English is spoken all over the world.” Folosim pasivul când acțiunea contează mai mult decât cine o face.
text.en: The passive: object + to be + past participle (+ by agent): "English is spoken all over the world." We use it when the action matters more than who does it.

text.ro: Present: is / are + participiu („Apples are grown by farmers”). Past: was / were + participiu („The window was broken by Tom”).
text.en: Present: is / are + participle ("Apples are grown by farmers"). Past: was / were + participle ("The window was broken by Tom").

text.ro: Din activ în pasiv: „Farmers grow apples.” → „Apples are grown by farmers.” Obiectul devine subiect, iar to be se acordă cu el.
text.en: From active to passive: "Farmers grow apples." → "Apples are grown by farmers." The object becomes the subject and to be agrees with it.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.passive.8
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Citește mai întâi cuvântul-semnal: every day, usually → present simple; now, at the moment, Look! → present continuous.
text.en: Read the signal word first: every day, usually → present simple; now, at the moment, Look! → present continuous.

text.ro: yesterday, last week, in 2019, ago → past simple; since, for, so far, never → present perfect.
text.en: yesterday, last week, in 2019, ago → past simple; since, for, so far, never → present perfect.

text.ro: Apoi verifică forma: auxiliarul (am / is / are, have / has, did) și verbul (cu -ing, cu -ed, participiu). O formă greșită se vede imediat.
text.en: Then check the form: the auxiliary (am / is / are, have / has, did) and the verb (-ing, -ed, participle). A wrong form is easy to spot.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.tenses.8
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Who pentru persoane: „The girl who lives next door is my friend.” Which / that pentru lucruri: „The book that I read was good.”
text.en: Who for people: "The girl who lives next door is my friend." Which / that for things: "The book that I read was good."

text.ro: Where pentru locuri: „This is the town where I was born.” Whose arată posesia: „The man whose car was stolen called the police.”
text.en: Where for places: "This is the town where I was born." Whose shows possession: "The man whose car was stolen called the police."

text.ro: Nu repetăm subiectul: nu „The man who he called”, ci „The man who called”. Cu whose nu mai punem un alt posesiv.
text.en: We do not repeat the subject: not "The man who he called" but "The man who called". After whose we do not add another possessive.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.relative.8
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: După enjoy, finish, mind, suggest, look forward to folosim -ing: „I enjoy listening to music.” „We finished painting.”
text.en: After enjoy, finish, mind, suggest, look forward to we use -ing: "I enjoy listening to music." "We finished painting."

text.ro: După want, decide, hope, promise, would like folosim to + verb: „She wants to be a doctor.” „He decided to ride his bike.”
text.en: After want, decide, hope, promise, would like we use to + verb: "She wants to be a doctor." "He decided to ride his bike."

text.ro: După prepoziții folosim -ing: „good at playing”, „interested in learning”. După modale și let / make: verb de bază: „Let’s play.” „She makes me clean.”
text.en: After prepositions we use -ing: "good at playing", "interested in learning". After modals and let / make: the base verb: "Let’s play." "She makes me clean."

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.patterns.8
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Reproducem ce a spus cineva: „Tom said that he was tired.” Pronumele se schimbă (I → he / she), iar timpul „coboară” cu un pas.
text.en: We report what somebody said: "Tom said that he was tired." Pronouns change (I → he / she) and the tense moves one step back.

text.ro: Present simple → past simple („I like pizza” → „she liked pizza”). Present continuous → past continuous („I am playing” → „he was playing”). Will → would.
text.en: Present simple → past simple ("I like pizza" → "she liked pizza"). Present continuous → past continuous ("I am playing" → "he was playing"). Will → would.

text.ro: Say + that: „She said that she was busy.” Tell + persoană: „He told me that he was ill.” Nu spunem „He said me”.
text.en: Say + that: "She said that she was busy." Tell + person: "He told me that he was ill." We do not say "He said me".

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.reported.8
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Cu run: run out of (a rămâne fără), run into (a întâlni din întâmplare). Cu take: take off (a decola), take after (a semăna cu), take up (a începe un hobby).
text.en: With run: run out of, run into (meet by chance). With take: take off, take after (be similar to), take up (start a hobby).

text.ro: Cu put: put off (a amâna), put up with (a suporta). Cu look: look up (a căuta în dicționar), look forward to (a aștepta cu plăcere).
text.en: With put: put off (postpone), put up with (tolerate). With look: look up (in a dictionary), look forward to (wait with pleasure).

text.ro: Altele: get on with (a te înțelege cu), carry on (a continua), break down (a se strica), figure out (a descoperi). Învață-le în propoziții.
text.en: Others: get on with (have good relations with), carry on (continue), break down (stop working), figure out (work out). Learn them in sentences.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.phrasal.8
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Used to și modale de probabilitate
title.en: Used to and modals of probability

text.ro: Used to + verb = ceva ce se făcea des în trecut și nu mai este adevărat: „I used to play with toy cars.” Întrebare / negativ: „Did you use to…?” „We didn’t use to…”
text.en: Used to + verb = something that often happened in the past and is no longer true: "I used to play with toy cars." Question / negative: "Did you use to…?" "We didn’t use to…"

text.ro: Be used to + -ing = obișnuit cu: „I am used to getting up early.” Nu confunda cele două.
text.en: Be used to + -ing = accustomed to: "I am used to getting up early." Do not confuse the two.

text.ro: Probabilitate: must be (aproape sigur) „He must be happy.” might / may (posibil) „It might rain.” can’t be (imposibil) „She can’t be at school, she is on holiday.”
text.en: Probability: must be (almost sure) "He must be happy." might / may (possible) "It might rain." can’t be (impossible) "She can’t be at school, she is on holiday."

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.usedto.8
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

text.ro: Prefixe care dau sens opus: un- (unhappy, unfair), dis- (disagree, dishonest), im- (impossible, impolite), in- (incorrect), ir- (irregular).
text.en: Prefixes that give the opposite meaning: un- (unhappy, unfair), dis- (disagree, dishonest), im- (impossible, impolite), in- (incorrect), ir- (irregular).

text.ro: Sufixe pentru adjective: -ful (careful, helpful), -less (useless, homeless), -y (sunny, funny), -able (enjoyable).
text.en: Suffixes for adjectives: -ful (careful, helpful), -less (useless, homeless), -y (sunny, funny), -able (enjoyable).

text.ro: Sufixe pentru substantive și adverbe: -ness (sadness), -ment (agreement), -ion (invention), -er / -or (teacher, visitor), -ly (quickly, happily). Citește propoziția ca să afli ce parte de vorbire îți trebuie.
text.en: Suffixes for nouns and adverbs: -ness (sadness), -ment (agreement), -ion (invention), -er / -or (teacher, visitor), -ly (quickly, happily). Read the sentence to see which part of speech you need.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.grammar.wordform.8
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.ro: Cum citim texte informative și interviuri
title.en: How to read informative texts and interviews

text.ro: Găsește ideea principală a fiecărui paragraf: de obicei se află în prima sau în ultima propoziție.
text.en: Find the main idea of each paragraph: it is usually in the first or the last sentence.

text.ro: Atenție la pasiv („was started”, „is used”) și la condiționale („If we take…, we will…”): ele spun ce se întâmplă sau ce se va întâmpla.
text.en: Watch for the passive ("was started", "is used") and conditionals ("If we take…, we will…"): they say what happens or will happen.

text.ro: La adevărat / fals caută în text cifre, nume, negații (not, never). O singură negație schimbă răspunsul.
text.en: For true / false look in the text for numbers, names and negatives (not, never). A single negative changes the answer.

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.read.8
provenance.author: Ludiko
provenance.notes: original explanation drafted for the competence; awaiting review by an English teacher

title.en: Opinions, phone calls and formal emails

text.ro: Opinii: „In my opinion…”, „I think…”, „What do you think about…?” Acord: „I agree with you.” Dezacord politicos: „I’m afraid I don’t agree.”
text.en: Opinions: "In my opinion…", "I think…", "What do you think about…?" Agreeing: "I agree with you." Disagreeing politely: "I’m afraid I don’t agree."

text.ro: La telefon: „Hello, this is Maria speaking.” „Can I speak to Dan, please?” „Sorry, could you speak up?” Sfat: „If I were you, I’d talk to your teacher.”
text.en: On the phone: "Hello, this is Maria speaking." "Can I speak to Dan, please?" "Sorry, could you speak up?" Advice: "If I were you, I’d talk to your teacher."

text.ro: E-mail formal: începem cu „Dear Mr Popa,” și încheiem cu „Yours sincerely,” sau „Best wishes,”. Reclamăm politicos: „Excuse me, this phone doesn’t work. Can I change it?”
text.en: Formal email: we start with "Dear Mr Popa," and finish with "Yours sincerely," or "Best wishes,". We complain politely: "Excuse me, this phone doesn’t work. Can I change it?"

provenance.title: Explanation for eng.func.opinion.8
provenance.author: Ludiko
